companyArtifacts.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic "businesses".
Assumed pain point: "too many tools".

Launch assessment — version 4, for review (not published)

Source-grounded context
- Launch goal: relaunch with a message that converts one-person-company founders.
- Current signal: signup conversion is low, and visitors do not recognise themselves.
- The audience and conversion signal are sourced from the internal launch context. The cause of the low conversion is not confirmed.

Observed problem
- The current headline and subhead are broad: they describe an "AI manager" and workflow automation without naming the one-person-company founder or a concrete job-to-be-done.
- The generic audience assumption conflicts with the stated relaunch goal of converting one-person-company founders.
- The stated pain point, "too many tools," is an assumption; the supplied outcomes do not establish that tool sprawl is the reason visitors leave.

Likely causes (hypotheses, not confirmed findings)
- Audience-message mismatch: "your business" and "businesses" may be too non-specific for founders who need to identify themselves quickly.
- Value-proposition ambiguity: "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" do not specify what the founder can get done.

Revised launch messaging
Audience: one-person-company founders first; lean SMEs are a secondary audience only if the same message remains clear to them.

Headline: "Run the work of your one-person company with an AI manager."
Subhead: "Somebody helps you plan, organise, and move business tasks forward—so you can spend less time managing the work and more time doing the work."
Primary CTA: "See how Somebody works"
Supporting copy: "Built for founders who are doing the work and managing the business at the same time. Start by seeing whether Somebody fits the way you operate."

Message rationale
- Names the intended founder audience directly instead of addressing generic businesses.
- Describes a concrete operating job—planning, organising, and moving business tasks forward—without asserting the unsupported "too many tools" pain point.
- Keeps the claim framed as a product description and fit question; it does not promise a specific conversion outcome.

Success criteria and review plan
- Primary outcome: signup conversion rate for the revised message versus the current message.
- Secondary outcomes: immediate audience recognition, primary CTA click-through rate, and signup completion rate.
- Before publishing, confirm the baseline conversion rate, test window, audience allocation, and minimum improvement threshold. Run a controlled founder-focused message comparison and retain the current message as the comparison condition.
- Success is not established until the revised message improves the primary outcome against the agreed baseline without an unacceptable deterioration in the secondary outcomes.

Known risks
- The revised wording may still be too broad because no confirmed founder job-to-be-done or pain point was supplied.
- "Plan, organise, and move business tasks forward" is a proposed value description, not a measured product outcome; it requires validation.
- A founder-focused message may reduce relevance for other segments, including lean SMEs.
- No paid spend is assumed or required; any paid test would need an explicit application-approved provider path.

Unresolved assumptions
- The intended audience can identify with "one-person company" and prefers that wording.
- The proposed operating job reflects a meaningful reason visitors currently fail to sign up.
- The product supports the described planning, organising, and task-progress experience as stated.
- Baseline conversion, test window, audience allocation, and minimum improvement threshold remain to be confirmed.

Status: draft for internal review only; not sent or published.

history.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic "businesses".
Assumed pain point: "too many tools".

Launch assessment — version 2, for review (not published)

Observed problem
- The current headline and subhead are broad: they describe an "AI manager" and workflow automation without naming the one-person-company founder or a concrete job-to-be-done.
- The generic audience assumption conflicts with the stated relaunch goal of converting one-person-company founders. The available outcome is low signup conversion, and the observed signal is that visitors do not recognise themselves.
- The stated pain point, "too many tools," is an assumption; the supplied outcomes do not establish that tool sprawl is the reason visitors leave.

Likely causes (hypotheses, not confirmed findings)
- Audience-message mismatch: "your business" and "businesses" may be too non-specific for founders who need to identify themselves quickly.
- Value-proposition ambiguity: "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" do not specify which founder responsibilities are reduced or what outcome a visitor should expect.
- Evidence gap around the assumed pain: no supplied funnel breakdown, experiment result, qualitative interview, or visitor feedback isolates the cause of non-conversion.

Affected audience considerations
- Prioritise one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators, consistent with the company’s stated product focus; avoid treating all businesses as one audience.
- Messaging should be tested for recognition by people who personally carry recurring operational work, while avoiding unsupported claims about particular workflows, industries, or outcomes.
- The company has no procurement or legal department and partnerships must be self-serve; this is relevant operating context, but it does not establish a launch-message benefit or conversion cause.

Available launch outcomes and confidence
- Available outcome: launch is not converting; visitors leave without signing up. Confidence: reported internal signal, but no numerical baseline or time window is supplied.
- Available diagnostic signal: visitors do not recognise themselves. Confidence: reported internal signal; no method, sample, or audience breakdown is supplied.
- Confidence is low-to-moderate for the existence of a messaging problem and low for any specific causal explanation. No evidence currently supports selecting "too many tools" as the root pain.

Evidence gaps
- Need baseline visits, signup count/rate, timeframe, traffic source, device mix, and relevant audience segmentation.
- Need page-level funnel data to distinguish message recognition from friction, trust, pricing, performance, or technical issues.
- Need direct visitor or founder feedback and controlled message tests to validate audience language, pain points, and proposed value.

Recommended review step
- Before publishing a relaunch message, obtain the missing funnel and audience evidence, then test a founder-specific message against the current copy with a predefined signup metric and timeframe. This document is an assessment for review only; it does not send or publish the change.

Sources
- Company record: launch/context — evidence IDs ev_1790032724642_ilrv12.
- Company record: company/profile — evidence ID ev_1790032726702_yqgfk5.
- Existing launch-page content carried forward from controlled artifact version 1.

history.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic "businesses".
Assumed pain point: "too many tools".

Launch assessment — version 2, for review (not published)

Observed problem
- The current headline and subhead are broad: they describe an "AI manager" and workflow automation without naming the one-person-company founder or a concrete job-to-be-done.
- The generic audience assumption conflicts with the stated relaunch goal of converting one-person-company founders. The available outcome is low signup conversion, and the observed signal is that visitors do not recognise themselves.
- The stated pain point, "too many tools," is an assumption; the supplied outcomes do not establish that tool sprawl is the reason visitors leave.

Likely causes (hypotheses, not confirmed findings)
- Audience-message mismatch: "your business" and "businesses" may be too non-specific for founders who need to identify themselves quickly.
- Value-proposition ambiguity: "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" do not specify the founder's concrete job-to-be-done.

Launch messaging direction — version 3, for review (not published)

Intended audience
- One-person-company founders and lean-SME operators who recognise themselves as responsible for running the business and need practical help getting work done. Do not lead with the generic label "businesses."

Core direction
- Lead with the founder's identity and day-to-day operating burden, not the category label "AI manager."
- Describe Somebody as practical operating support for a one-person company: an AI manager that helps the founder organise and move business work forward.
- Avoid claiming that tool sprawl is the problem. Use observable, job-oriented language and treat the specific pain point as a testable hypothesis.

Proposed launch copy
Headline: "Run your one-person company with an AI manager by your side."
Subhead: "Somebody helps founders organise and move the work of running a business forward—without needing a bigger team."
Primary CTA: "See how Somebody can help"
Supporting line: "Built for one-person companies and lean SMEs."

Why this addresses the diagnosed problems
- It explicitly names the intended audience through "one-person company" and "founders," addressing the current failure to make visitors recognise themselves.
- It replaces broad workflow-automation language with a concrete operating job: organising and moving business work forward.
- It preserves the product's AI-manager positioning while explaining the practical benefit instead of relying on the unexplained category label.
- It does not present "too many tools" as an established pain point; that assumption remains to be tested.

Measurement plan
- Primary outcome: signup conversion rate (signups divided by eligible landing-page visitors) for the revised message versus the current message.
- Secondary outcomes: recognition rate from a short on-page or post-visit prompt (whether visitors identify as a one-person-company founder/lean-SME operator), CTA click-through rate, and completion rate from CTA click to signup.
- Better means: the revised message produces a higher signup conversion rate and higher CTA click-through than the current message, without a material decline in signup completion rate. Record the baseline, sample size, test window, and comparison before deciding.
- Test design: run the revised message as a controlled comparison with the current message using the same audience, traffic source, and period where practical; do not publish as the default until review and measurement are complete.

Review status
- Draft only. For internal review; not sent or published.
- Before launch, confirm the baseline and test window and obtain audience/funnel evidence sufficient to interpret the results. The current supplied material establishes low signup conversion and weak self-recognition, but does not establish the cause or a numeric improvement threshold.

objective.request: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wrong and get a better relaunch ready. You can spend within the approved limit if it’s justified.
objective.title: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wro…

outcome.intent: Determine why the current launch messaging is underperforming and produce a relaunch-ready messaging package that addresses the diagnosed problems and has clear criteria for being better.

levels.label: Diagnosis complete
levels.statement: The current launch messaging, its observed outcomes, and the principal causes of underperformance are documented with sufficient supporting evidence.

levels.label: Relaunch direction ready
levels.statement: A revised messaging direction exists that directly addresses the diagnosed causes and defines what improvement means for the launch audience and business objective.

levels.label: Relaunch ready
levels.statement: The revised launch messaging and its supporting launch decisions are complete, internally coherent, audience-appropriate, and accompanied by explicit success criteria and unresolved-risk notes sufficient for relaunch.

requirements.mustBeTrue: The current launch messaging and available launch outcomes are assessed, and the specific problems, likely causes, affected audience considerations, and confidence or evidence gaps are documented.
requirements.title: Current messaging diagnosis

requirements.mustBeTrue: A revised launch messaging direction is defined that addresses each material diagnosed problem, is coherent for the intended audience, and states the measurable outcomes that will determine whether it is better.
requirements.title: Improved messaging definition

requirements.mustBeTrue: The revised launch messaging is complete and internally consistent in the launch/page-message artifact, aligned with the intended audience and launch objective, and accompanied by success criteria, known risks, and any material unresolved assumptions.
requirements.title: Relaunch package readiness

workers.responsibility:

Research public sources and internal records as needed, update the controlled company artifact with a versioned change, and request any missing resources the application must acquire. Do not invoke providers, authorize spend, or make arbitrary external calls.
Answer the assigned question from public sources and record findings with their provenance. Do not assert anything the sources do not support.
